subtitle: A cobbler-poet carves a city beyond fear from the dust of Banaras

panels.shot: wide, low-angle dusk view of Ravidas at his roadside cobbler stall, city of Banaras hazy behind him like a distant fortress
panels.action: Ravidas sits cross-legged by a simple cobbler’s stall on a Banaras lane, leather tools laid out before him, as the towering city walls and temple spires loom in the smoky distance.

dialogue.text: In fifteenth-century Banaras, where caste ruled every doorway, a cobbler named Ravidas dared to sing of Begampura—a city with no fear, no taxes, no second-class souls.

i18n.hi: पंद्रहवीं सदी के बनारस में, जहाँ हर चौखट पर जात का पहरा, वहाँ चमार रैदास ने बेगमपुरा गाया—एक नगर बिना डर, बिना लगान, बिना अधम जनों के।

panels.shot: slow push-in from street chaos to intimate close-up of Ravidas’s hands working leather
panels.action: Crowded lanes swirl with merchants and pilgrims as Ravidas, calm amid the bustle, bends over a worn sandal, his calloused fingers stitching carefully in the soft light.

dialogue.text: The records do not give us Ravidas’s exact birth year. They give us something sharper—his voice, rising from Banaras’ leather-working world, where Chamars laboured at the edge of respect.

i18n.hi: रैदास की सही जन्मतिथि दर्ज नहीं, पर उनकी आवाज़ दर्ज है—बनारस के चमड़े के काम से उठती, उस दुनिया से जहाँ चमार इज़्ज़त की हद पर मेहनत करते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot, Ravidas seated at his stall, brahmin customers passing by him with subtle distance
panels.action: Ravidas sits near the road with simple dignity as finely dressed men step around his stall, some avoiding his shadow, the sacred river glittering far beyond.

dialogue.text: To mend shoes was to carry the mark of leather, of impurity, in a world of strict hierarchies. But Ravidas did not only shape sandals. He shaped questions—about who truly belongs.

i18n.hi: जूते जोड़ना मतलब चमड़े की छाप, ऊँच–नीच के सख्त समाज में ‘अपवित्र’ का निशान। पर रैदास सिर्फ सैंडल नहीं, सवाल भी गढ़ते थे—कि असली अपनापन किसका है।

panels.shot: interior hut, close-up of Ravidas’s face lit by lamp as he chants, background simple family space
panels.action: In a modest hut, a clay lamp spills warm light on Ravidas’s thoughtful face as he sits on the floor, eyes half-closed, chanting softly into the quiet night.

dialogue.text: From this small, dim space in Banaras came songs that crossed regions. The Guru Granth Sahib preserves forty-one of them—words that carried the weight of a cobbler’s life and a seeker’s fire.

i18n.hi: बनारस की एक छोटी, धुँआली कोठरी से निकलीं वे रचनाएँ जो दूर इलाकों तक पहुँचीं। गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में उनकी इकतालीस बाणी है—एक मोची की ज़िंदगी और एक साधक की ज्वाला से भरे शब्द।

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot of Ravidas by the Ganga ghats, priests and commoners around, subtle distance between him and ritual center
panels.action: At the stone ghats of the Ganga, priests perform rituals near the steps while Ravidas stands a little apart, watching the water flow, his hands folded loosely.

dialogue.text: In the north Indian Sant tradition, Ravidas’s voice joined those who turned from ritual to inner devotion. Yet his path was marked by something more—life under caste exclusion, felt every day.

i18n.hi: उत्तर भारत की संत परंपरा में रैदास की आवाज़ उन लोगों से जुड़ती है जो कर्मकांड छोड़ अंतर भक्ति की ओर मुड़े। पर उनकी राह पर एक और घाव था—रोज़–रोज़ महसूस होती जात की बेरुख़ी।

panels.shot: close-up on Ravidas’s eyes, background dissolving into faint outlines of palaces and tax collectors
panels.action: Ravidas looks up from his work, eyes distant, as the background blurs into ghostly silhouettes of city gates, palace towers, and stern officials counting coins.

dialogue.text: Cities promised safety, wealth, splendour. They also brought anxiety—taxes, tolls, the fear of guards at every gate. For a low-caste cobbler, the city was shelter and cage at once.

i18n.hi: शहरों ने सुरक्षा, धन, चमक का वादा किया, पर साथ ही डर भी—लगान, चुंगी, हर फाटक पर सिपाहियों की दहशत। नीची जात के मोची के लिए शहर ओट भी था, जेल भी।

panels.shot: intimate shot inside hut, Ravidas composing, a palm-leaf manuscript nearby, his tools set aside
panels.action: Ravidas sits cross-legged with his cobbler’s tools pushed aside, a palm-leaf manuscript resting by his knee as he lifts his chin and begins to intone a new verse.

dialogue.text: And so Ravidas began to sing of another city. Not Banaras with its taxes, or fort towns with guarded walls—but Begampura, a place that broke the old rules of belonging.

i18n.hi: तब रैदास ने एक और शहर गाना शुरू किया। न बनारस अपने करों वाला, न किलों की दीवारों वाला—बल्कि बेगमपुरा, जो अपनाने के पुराने नियम तोड़ दे।

panels.shot: semi-symbolic wide shot, Ravidas seated, with a faint visionary city forming around him in light
panels.action: As Ravidas chants, the dark hut around him softens into an imagined glow, faint outlines of streets and houses appearing like a dream city rising from his words.

dialogue.text: Begampura shahar ko nāu… dukhu andohu nahi tihī thāu.

i18n.hi: बेगमपुरा शहर को नाउँ… दुखु अँदोहु नाही तिही ठाउँ।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Ravidas, visionary streets showing people of many backgrounds walking together
panels.action: The dream city around Ravidas clarifies into peaceful streets where people of different dress and status walk side by side, no guards at gates, faces calm and unhurried.

dialogue.text: “Begampura, that is the name of the town; there is no suffering there, no fear.” In his verse, no one trembles before tax men, no one is pushed aside as less than whole.

i18n.hi: “बेगमपुरा, यही उस नगर का नाम है; वहाँ न दुख है, न डर।” उसकी बाणी में कोई महसूलदार से काँपता नहीं, कोई आधा–अधूरा मानकर धकेला नहीं जाता।

panels.shot: medium shot, Ravidas singing to a small, mixed gathering of workers and ordinary folk in a lane
panels.action: On a dusty lane, Ravidas sits on a low platform, singing as a circle of artisans, labourers and women listen, some with tools still in hand, drawn into the song.

dialogue.text: Begampura is not a blueprint for bricks and stone. It is a challenge: can a city exist without second-class citizens, without the tight fist of revenue and caste at every turn?

i18n.hi: बेगमपुरा ईंट–पत्थर का नक़्शा नहीं, एक चुनौती है: क्या कोई शहर बिना दोयम दर्जे के नागरिकों के, बिना हर मोड़ पर राजस्व और जात के शिकंजे के हो सकता है?

panels.shot: close-up of a listener’s face, moved, then back to Ravidas’s steady presence
panels.action: A young listener’s eyes shine with wonder as they turn from the imagined city in their mind back to Ravidas, whose steady, grounded gaze returns them to the dusty street.

dialogue.text: In a world where most accepted caste as fate, Ravidas’s words bent that future. He did not draft laws; he named a city where fear itself had no right to live.

i18n.hi: एक ऐसे ज़माने में जब ज़्यादातर लोग जात को किस्मत मान चुके थे, रैदास के शब्दों ने उस किस्मत को मोड़ दिया। उन्होंने क़ानून नहीं लिखे, उन्होंने एक ऐसा शहर नाम लिया जहाँ डर को रहने का हक़ ही नहीं।

panels.shot: symbolic split scene, one half showing royal tax collection, other half Begampura’s open gate
panels.action: A stylized frame shows stern officials weighing coins before a tense crowd on one side, while on the other an open gateway leads into Begampura’s calm streets, unguarded and inviting.

dialogue.text: Ravidas speaks of a place where kings do not impose crushing levies, where no one is harassed for dues. His city is less a place on a map than a measure of justice.

i18n.hi: रैदास उस जगह की बात करते हैं जहाँ राजा कुचलने वाली लगान नहीं थोपते, जहाँ किसी को बकाया के नाम पर सताया नहीं जाता। उनका शहर नक़्शे का ठिकाना कम, न्याय का पैमाना ज़्यादा है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Ravidas declining reverence, seated plainly among listeners
panels.action: A listener bows deeply before Ravidas, but he gestures gently for them to sit beside him, flattening the distance between teacher and taught.

dialogue.text: Later stories would wrap Ravidas with more miracles, more royal visits, more disciples. Scholars sift these tales with care—but Begampura stands firm in the older, attested songs.

i18n.hi: बाद की कहानियाँ रैदास के चारों ओर और चमत्कार, और राजा–मुलाक़ातें, और चेले जोड़ती गईं। विद्वान इन कथाओं को परखते हैं—पर बेगमपुरा तो पुरानी, प्रमाणित बाणियों में मज़बूती से खड़ा है।

panels.shot: interior scriptorium-style scene, anonymous scribes copying verses, Ravidas’s figure faintly in background
panels.action: In a simple room, scribes sit with reed pens and sheets, carefully copying verses as a faint image of Ravidas singing appears like memory in the background.

dialogue.text: By 1604, when the Guru Granth Sahib was compiled, forty-one hymns of Ravidas had travelled far enough, reliably enough, to be gathered into Sikh scripture as part of a shared spiritual canon.

i18n.hi: १६०४ तक, जब गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब तैयार हुआ, रैदास की इकतालीस बाणियाँ इतनी दूर और भरोसेमंद सफ़र कर चुकी थीं कि साझा आध्यात्मिक धरोहर के रूप में सिख धर्मग्रंथ में शामिल हो सकें।

panels.shot: close-up on a manuscript leaf showing Ravidas’s name and lines of verse, hands reverently turning it
panels.action: Hands gently turn a manuscript leaf where Ravidas’s name appears beside flowing lines of verse, the page lit like a precious bridge across time.

dialogue.text: From Banaras’ leather lanes to the pages of the Guru Granth Sahib, his words crossed boundaries that his body could not. The cobbler’s song became part of everyday prayer.

i18n.hi: बनारस की चमड़ा गलियों से गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब के पन्नों तक, उसकी बाणी उन हदों को पार कर गई जिन्हें उसका शरीर नहीं कर सकता था। मोची का गीत रोज़ की अरदास का हिस्सा बन गया।

panels.shot: modern symbolic montage: faint outlines of contemporary Ravidassia gathering overlaying Ravidas singing
panels.action: Ravidas’s singing figure fades into a semi-transparent scene of a modern congregation, people standing together in a hall as his verses are sung, linking past and present.

dialogue.text: Today, communities who honour Ravidas wrestle with his legacy, with identity and dignity. Historians trace transmission lines; devotees hear in Begampura a promise still not fully kept.

i18n.hi: आज रैदास को मानने वाले समुदाय उनकी विरासत, अपनी पहचान और इज़्ज़त से जूझते हैं। इतिहासकार बाणी की राहें तलाशते हैं; भक्त बेगमपुरा में अब भी अधूरा वादा सुनते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Ravidas back at his stall, visionary Begampura hovering above the city like a gentle mirage
panels.action: Ravidas returns to his cobbler’s stall on the Banaras street, stitching quietly as above the city a soft mirage of Begampura hangs in the sky, half-dream, half-demand.

dialogue.text: No stone city of Begampura was ever founded. Yet every time someone refuses fear and exclusion, they walk a little of its streets—the ones a cobbler once dared to name from the margins.

i18n.hi: पत्थर की बेगमपुरा कभी बसाई नहीं गई। पर जब–जब कोई डर और बहिष्कार को ठुकराता है, वह उसकी गलियों में थोड़ा चल ही लेता है—उन गलियों में जिन्हें एक मोची ने किनारों से नाम लेने की हिम्मत की थी।

subtitle_i18n.en: A cobbler-poet carves a city beyond fear from the dust of Banaras
subtitle_i18n.hi: जोताजुती कवि बनारस की धूल से डर रहित शहर गढ़ता है
